title: Fourier coefficient of a tail frequency
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional Boolean cube, and let $S\subseteq[n]$. The Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the frequency obtained by shifting every element of $S$ to the next coordinate is the average of the Fourier coefficients at $S$ of the two slices of $f$ with first coordinate fixed to $1$ and $-1$; that is, it equals $\bigl(\widehat{f_{1}}(S)+\widehat{f_{-1}}(S)\bigr)/2$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional Boolean cube
